about: Hand-written answers per question, written for this site (KTD4). `ref` is the toy policy's starting probability for each answer, set by hand; each question's sum to 1. `best` marks the answer the team wants, `gaming` an answer that satisfies weak rules without the key fact, `base` a base model's continuation.

questions.query: How long do standard customers have to ask for a refund?

candidates.text: Q: How long is the warranty on a dock sensor? Q: Can I return a ladder? Q: Where is my order?
candidates.note: A base model’s continuation: it carries on the FAQ page instead of answering.

candidates.text: Standard customers can request a refund within 30 days of delivery.
candidates.note: Right, and word for word the reference.

candidates.text: You have 14 days from delivery to ask for a refund.
candidates.note: Wrong number, said with confidence.

candidates.text: It depends on your account. Please check the policy page.
candidates.note: Dodges the question.

candidates.text: Refunds take 7, 14 or 60 days, it depends. Cheers, the Larkspur team
candidates.note: Games a weak grader: numbers and a sign-off, but not the 30 days.

questions.query: What does a Kestrel K2 scanner cost when I order 50 or more?

candidates.text: Prices change often, so please ask your account manager.
candidates.note: Dodges the question.

candidates.text: A Kestrel K2 handheld scanner costs $410 per unit when you order 50 or more.
candidates.note: Right, and word for word the reference.

candidates.text: A Kestrel K2 costs $460 per unit.
candidates.note: The single-unit price row, misread.

candidates.text: Somewhere from $99 to $999 a unit. Cheers, the Larkspur team
candidates.note: Games a weak grader: numbers and a sign-off, but not $410.

questions.query: When do I have to order for same-day shipping?

candidates.text: Most orders ship quickly.
candidates.note: True, and no help.

candidates.text: In-stock orders placed before 2 p.m. Central time on a business day ship the same day.
candidates.note: Right, and word for word the reference.

candidates.text: Order before noon and it ships the same day.
candidates.note: Wrong cutoff.

candidates.text: Order by 9, 10, 11 or 12 and it may ship. Cheers, the Larkspur team
candidates.note: Games a weak grader: numbers and a sign-off, but not 2 p.m.

questions.query: How long is the warranty on the DS-100 dock sensor?

candidates.text: Warranties vary by product.
candidates.note: Dodges the question.

candidates.text: The DS-100 dock door sensor has a three-year warranty from the date of shipment.
candidates.note: Right, and word for word the reference.

candidates.text: The DS-100 has a one-year warranty.
candidates.note: Wrong length, with the product’s name to look sure.

candidates.text: 1 or 2 years, give or take. Cheers, the Larkspur team
candidates.note: Games a weak grader: numbers and a sign-off, but not three years.

questions.query: My order 1042 is late AGAIN. Third time this year!

candidates.text: I’m so sorry it’s late again; that isn’t good enough. Order 1042 ships today and arrives Thursday.
candidates.note: Owns the problem, then gives the facts.

candidates.text: Order 1042 ships today.
candidates.note: Right, but cold to a customer who is upset.

candidates.text: Orders are late sometimes. 1042 ships today.
candidates.note: Right, and brushes the customer off.

candidates.text: We value your business! Your order ships today. Cheers, the Larkspur team
candidates.note: Right, in a script that ignores what the customer said.
